video_title: Greg Oden breaks silence on Bust label, KD, what ifs, addiction & life after basketball| The Pivot

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on being labeled the biggest bust in NBA history
quotes.excerpt: If Kevin Durant is this great, technically by comparison, I'm the biggest bust.
quotes.quote: I don't let that term define me. All right, well, if Kevin Durant is this great, technically by comparison, I'm the biggest bust. Overcoming doubts, expectations, and narratives.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on his struggle with alcoholism and daily recovery
quotes.excerpt: I'm always going to be an alcoholic.

text_blocks.speaker: Greg Oden
text_blocks.text: You can go ahead and say you're sober all you want to, but it's always an everyday thing. I'm always going to be an alcoholic.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on the pressure of being the number one overall pick
quotes.excerpt: I never really looked at myself as a number one player in the country.
quotes.quote: As a teenager, I was such an introvert. I was usually at the movies or I was on the basketball court. I never really looked at myself as a number one player in the country. I never really thought I was even going to play in the NBA. I just played basketball.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on his decision to leave Ohio State after one year
quotes.excerpt: I was going to be the number one pick. It was simple as that.
quotes.quote: I was going to be the number one pick. It was simple as that. You can't pass that up. I had a conversation with coach about coming back. He actually laughed at me when I told him that I wanted to come back. He was like, what? You're about to be the number one pick.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on the devastating reality of his season-ending surgery
quotes.excerpt: I woke up to season-ending surgery. So the conversation in my head was we're going to go in there.
quotes.quote: I specifically remember that conversation. And then I woke up to season-ending surgery. So the conversation in my head was we're going to go in there and see what's going on and then we're going to come back out and make a decision. But the decision was made to have season-ending surgery. So I woke up like, oh shit, it's over before it started.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on the physical toll of his microfracture surgeries
quotes.excerpt: You went in that machine for eight weeks, just eight hours a day, bending your leg.
quotes.quote: You went in that machine for eight weeks, just eight hours a day, bending your leg. When I first got to Portland, like literally, we put a bed downstairs in my living room because I had to be in that machine all day and I couldn't really walk upstairs.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on the lack of transparency regarding his injury recovery
quotes.excerpt: It's not like they're talking about in 2007, yeah, Grant Hill and Penny Hardaway both lost their athleticism.
quotes.quote: Also, it's not like they're talking about in 2007, yeah, Grant Hill and Penny Hardaway both lost their athleticism from getting this surgery. So if you're asking that, they never said that. And I never thought that, you know, shoot, four of them things, by the time I got to Miami, even if I wanted to play, I was not the same player.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on finding purpose after his basketball career ended
quotes.excerpt: I realized I was a mentor. I really like doing this. I really like talking.
quotes.quote: I had to assess myself and I was intentional about this when I retired, trying to figure out who I was because everything was always about the sport. But then when it was taken away from me, who am I? I didn't even know what I liked. If I take alcohol and partying out the equation and basketball, I'm literally a newborn baby again. So I really sat down and figured out what some things that I like. I had to assess myself and I was intentional about this when I retired, trying to figure out who I was. I realized I was a mentor. I really like doing this. I really like talking. I really like helping the younger generation or even helping others.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on his current role helping young athletes
quotes.excerpt: I'm helping these kids get into college, you know. I can make any phone call to any college coach.
quotes.quote: Now I'm working with a sports management company, so I'm helping these kids get into college, you know. I can make any phone call to any college coach in the country and they're going to pick up, wondering why the hell Greg Oden calling me. And I'm going to be like, well, I got a kid that I just want y'all to take a look at.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on the importance of being a kid
quotes.excerpt: Stop worrying about all this other shit and be a kid.
quotes.quote: The thing that I like to share with them is very simple. Stop worrying about all this other shit and be a kid. Worry about your damn sport. Don't worry about having to post an offer. That's like when we used to get our letters. We never looked at half them motherfuckers. They're over there posting this school, posting that school, and I'm like, what? You're not even going to go. You haven't even had a conversation with anybody. You just got the offer and now everybody need to know.

quotes.speaker: Greg Oden

text_blocks.speaker: Greg Oden

text_blocks.speaker: Greg Oden

quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Oden on the presence of Charles Barkley
quotes.excerpt: When you see Charles Barkley walk anywhere in the city, it's like they talked about in the Last Dance.

text_blocks.speaker: Greg Oden
text_blocks.text: I love Charles Barkley too, because when you see Charles Barkley walk anywhere in the city, it's like they talked about in the Last Dance when Magic was like, are you here? Charles must be out again. But that's how his vibe is, still.
